newsitem.title: USA: Intel takes swipe at Calif. proposal.
newsitem.headline: Intel takes swipe at Calif. proposal.

text.p: Intel Corp, the computer semiconductor maker, took a swipe at a proposed California law on Monday when it refused to make forward looking statements in its upcoming earnings report and cancelled a financial analysts meeting.
Intel is scheduled to report third quarter earnings on October 14. It cancelled the analysts meeting on October 31.

The ballot initiative, called Proposition 211, would make corporate executives and directors liable for losses and civil damages in shareholder lawsuits over statements, or omission of statements, regarding material facts related to companies.
Proponents of the measure say it will protect investors from securities fraud and spectacles such as the 1980s banking and loan debacle.

Opponents, including many of the state's high-tech firms like Intel, contend Proposition 211 will increase the number of frivolous lawsuits filed against them and render the federal securities "safe harbor" law useless.

"Although passage of this measure is uncertain, Intel does not intend to assume the risk of making forward-looking statements concerning the company's business outlook, the company said in a statement.
Californians will vote on the measure on November 5.
A recent poll commissioned by the anti-211 group found 25 percent of Californians surveyed in favor and 30 percent opposed, and 45 percent undecided.

High-tech companies feel the law would hit them particularly hard because so many of their businesses are based on upcoming products and services that are expected to reap huge financial returns. Sometimes, however, the products are superceded by innovations before they even get to market.
